data.name: Esper - Make You Live Again
data.detailed_description:
Esper - Make You Live Again is a kinetic novel in which Ryo Masaki tells his story whereas he was only a young student in an Esper academy.

The Espers are humans with special abilities. They can, when a person is suffering, share the pain and see the past and the memories of that person. Using their powers and their understanding of the problem, the Espers can help the person, and give them the will to live again.

Ryo tells what happened when he passed his exam to become a certified Esper and how these events impacted his life and the life of many others to the point that they changed him forever.

A kinetic novel?

Yes, Esper - Make You Live Again is a kinetic novel. You don't interact with the story, there's no choices or routes nor different endings. Simply sit down, set up the auto mode to your tastes and enjoy the story. You don't have to start over in order to see the good ending or to understand the last part of the story, everything is included in one playthrough.

How long is the story?

The story of Esper - Make You Live Again is about 90,000 words long. The rest depends on you, on how fast you can read, how long you will look at the characters and the places and listen to the music. Esper - Make You Live Again is not an experience designed to be either long, short or to last for a certain amount of time. This is an experience designed to be enjoyable.

What can I expect from Esper - Make You Live Again?

As a kinetic novel, Esper - Make You Live Again is not only a story. It's also a visual and audio experience. The journey Ryo made will take you to more than 20 locations, you'll meet 14 characters and you'll be rocked by a soundtrack of more than 35 minutes (17 tracks). Set a custom delay for the auto mode as well as the speed of the text and enjoy the story at your own pace in the comfort of your favorite armchair.

Soundtrack included

The soundtrack is available for free with each purchase of Esper - Make You Live Again. There's a jukebox available in-game and all the music files can also be retrieved in your installation folder, in Ogg Vorbis format. To find the soundtrack, navigate to your installation folder, then to /resources/app/soundtrack/.

reviews.review:
[h1]Brief[/h1]
Esper - Make You Live again is a pretty straight forward story telling game in the design of a Visual Novel, known as a Kinetic Novel. Offering various characters and scenes, it gives a pretty accurate depiction of what it would be like to be in this universe.

[h1]Pros[/h1]
- Good Story
- Decent Length (see Additional Comments)
- Chapter Select
- Good Options
- Good & Consistent Art
- Decent Music
- Has A Demo (Not many games do this anymore)

[h1]Cons[/h1]
- Lack of Story Choices (see Additional Comments)
- No "Text To Speech" reading/Voice Actor(s) (Not a major con, just be aware that youll need to read and not be read to)

[h1]Additional Comments[/h1]
I should mention that my play time for this game is well above and beyond what the actual game entails for a single playthrough. I helped Stoi with this game before release and because of that, my hours are pretty high. I would expect, depending on how fast you read and the like, to expect this game to last 4 hours. That said, take your time with it, enjoy what the story is telling you, re-read parts if necessary to fully grasp the entire thing. There is never a reason to rush through a good physical book, and there shouldn't be a reason either for wanting to rush through a visual book.

Now, this game was not designed to be a normal visual novel in the sense of player picking choices, I feel that it could have benefited this game quite a bit. There are quite a few things that I would have actually branched into, given the choice, instead of being railroaded down one particular path. This is by no means a major flaw of the game, but something I would like to see in any future novel games by Stoi. Even if it means only a few side branches that eventually go back to the main line.

[i]Note[/i]: The following is vague on purpose, to not spoil anything of the story. If I cannot be vague, it is marked as a spoiler. If there are any questions, feel free to comment on this review and I'll respond about the particulars as a spoiler.

There are also a few other things with this game that I would have liked to see in the long run but since the text system he was using wasn't overly sophisticated it was unable to be done within a reasonable amount of time. Some of the dialog could have been made larger in spots to indicate shouting, or text colors used to indicate some emotion, internal dialog, and the like. These in the long run are minor, but something I've personally enjoyed in other visual novels. I suppose it doesn't matter in the long run but these types of things can help. One thing this game does though is offer a pause in a spot of dialog, which is a really nice touch. Something I think could have been used elsewhere in the story to also offer that same nice effect that I got the very first time it shows up, such as after an ellipsis which is commonly used to indicate there being more, or hesitation, etc. Perhaps a future game could take these designs into consideration then to make the game that much better.

Additionally, some of the choices that I would have liked to see would be related to the overall characters in the story. I would have loved to some characters be chosen to talk to over the way the story tells it, or have the player choose not to talk to them at all. Some of them are definitely a bit odd and perhaps they're not everyone's preference to want to ever deal with, making the main character their own/themselves. After all of that, and the main characters event comes, it would also be interesting to see a choice be offered to enter before all of the dialog is gone through in that particular room. Beyond that particular rooms thing, being in the city and finding out about something so suddenly felt a bit forced to me. That could also have been an opportunity to delve into a player choice of choosing to pursue that something or to offer the player the chance to continue on with exploring the city, at least temporarily ignoring it.

It would have been nice too to actually have been given the choices of where you went from day to day, similar to how other visual novels/games handle it (thinking of Ace Attorney, or how Danganronpa handles it), even if it meant finding nothing there, or perhaps a random interaction or two, perhaps giving a bit of additional lore of the city, or fully understanding everything that was said and knowing exactly where you should go to advance the main story. This being added would have made the world, that is already lore rich as it is, that much better.

But perhaps I've typed enough. Overall, I really do enjoy the game and would recommend it. There is plenty to be earned from this game if you let it. It is worth the price of admission to get to experience what it's like to be an Esper, and very much look forward to seeing more of this universe in the future.
